terms.definition: A person, organisation or government body that can bear a role in relation to a property asset, agreement, authorisation or business activity.
terms.label: Party

terms.definition: An individual human party, for example an owner-occupier renting rooms, an individual investor or a resident.
terms.label: Person

terms.definition: A legal or business entity such as a company, trust, partnership, agency, franchisor, lender or insurer.
terms.label: Organisation

terms.definition: A public authority at federal, state or local level that legislates, regulates, registers, licenses, taxes or plans.
terms.label: Government body

terms.definition: A local government authority administering a planning scheme, development approvals, premises registration and local compliance.
terms.label: Local council

terms.definition: A government body that administers a regulatory regime, for example the Residential Tenancies Authority, the Australian Taxation Office or Consumer Affairs Victoria.
terms.label: Regulator

terms.definition: An organisation operating a commercial activity in property, such as a property-management agency, developer, operator or real-estate agency.
terms.label: Business

terms.definition: A business that manages properties on behalf of owners under management agreements, holding a rent roll and providing leasing, rent collection, inspection, maintenance and reporting services.
terms.label: Property management business

terms.definition: A context-dependent capacity a party bears in relation to a property, agreement or activity (owner, investor, operator, landlord, tenant, resident, property manager, lender, insurer, developer, adviser). Roles are named individuals of this class, bound to parties through participations.
terms.label: Role

terms.definition: The occurrence of a party bearing a role in a specific context (an agreement, property asset, development project or business), optionally bounded in time.
terms.label: Participation

terms.definition: A parcel of land, building, dwelling, rentable unit or commercial premises that can be owned, leased, developed or operated.
terms.label: Property asset

terms.definition: A legally identified parcel of land, described by a lot-on-plan and represented spatially in a cadastre.
terms.label: Land parcel

terms.definition: A structure on land, classified for building-code purposes and containing one or more dwellings or units.
terms.label: Building

terms.definition: A self-contained residential unit of accommodation, whether a detached house, apartment, duplex half, dual-key section or secondary dwelling.
terms.label: Dwelling

terms.definition: A room, studio, bed or tenancy unit let separately within a larger property, for example a rooming-house room, a coliving bed or a multi-tenant commercial unit.
terms.label: Rentable unit

terms.definition: Property occupied for business purposes such as retail, office, industrial, healthcare or warehouse use.
terms.label: Commercial premises

terms.definition: A collection of property assets held or managed together by an investor or business, including a property manager's rent roll.
terms.label: Portfolio

terms.definition: An identifier that denotes a property asset within some identification scheme (address, lot-on-plan, title reference, cadastral parcel identifier, G-NAF address identifier).
terms.label: Property identifier

terms.definition: A postal or geocoded street address identifying a property.
terms.label: Address

terms.definition: A Queensland-style legal land description consisting of a lot number and registered plan.
terms.label: Lot-on-plan identifier

terms.definition: The registered title identifier under which ownership and registered interests (mortgages, easements, covenants, leases, caveats) are recorded.
terms.label: Title reference

terms.definition: The identifier of a parcel in the spatial cadastral fabric.
terms.label: Cadastral parcel identifier

terms.definition: A geographic-legal area (nation, state, local government area, metropolitan region) within which a regulatory regime, tax rule or market statistic applies.
terms.label: Jurisdiction

terms.definition: A contract between two or more parties concerning the occupation, operation, management or use of a property asset, carrying term, rent, permitted use and allocation of obligations and risks.
terms.label: Agreement

terms.definition: A general tenancy agreement under which a tenant rents whole residential premises from a lessor.
terms.label: Residential tenancy agreement

terms.definition: An agreement under which a resident rents a room and shares facilities with a provider; in Queensland the prescribed form under the Residential Tenancies and Rooming Accommodation Act 2008.
terms.label: Rooming accommodation agreement

terms.definition: A lease from the property owner to an operator who then sublets to residents or occupants; the operator pays fixed rent regardless of occupancy.
terms.label: Head lease (master lease)

terms.definition: A letting by a head tenant or operator to an end tenant, resident or occupant of all or part of premises held under a head lease.
terms.label: Sublease

terms.definition: An agreement under which an operator or property manager manages accommodation or property for an owner in return for a fee and/or revenue or profit share, without fixed head rent.
terms.label: Management agreement

terms.definition: A lease of residential property to a company for occupation by its staff, typically furnished and serviced to a higher standard at a premium rent.
terms.label: Corporate lease

terms.definition: A lease of commercial premises between a lessor and a business lessee, characterised by lease type (gross, net, triple net), term, rent reviews, permitted use and outgoings allocation.
terms.label: Commercial lease

terms.definition: A provision within an agreement that allocates a specific right, obligation or contingency, such as subletting permission, break rights, rent escalation, make-good or co-tenancy relief.
terms.label: Contract clause

terms.definition: A commercial-lease clause allowing a tenant to reduce rent or exercise other rights if an anchor tenant leaves or occupancy falls below an agreed level.
terms.label: Co-tenancy clause

terms.definition: An express provision granting the tenant or operator authority to sublet or license the premises to others.
terms.label: Subletting permission clause

terms.definition: The assignment of a category of property outgoing (taxes, insurance, maintenance, common-area costs, capital expenditure, utilities) to the party in a given role under a lease type.
terms.label: Outgoing allocation

terms.definition: A coherent body of rules administered by a regulator under legislation in a jurisdiction that applies to an operating model or accommodation type, may set occupancy thresholds and may require authorisations before operation.
terms.label: Regulatory regime

terms.definition: A named statute, regulation, planning provision, code or ruling that establishes a regulatory regime or rule.
terms.label: Legislation

terms.definition: An information artefact with legal effect, such as legislation, a prescribed form or a planning-scheme provision.
terms.label: Legal instrument

terms.definition: A form mandated by a regulator for a specified agreement or notice, such as Queensland's Form R18 rooming accommodation agreement.
terms.label: Prescribed form

terms.definition: A specific requirement, restriction or entitlement within a regime that has effective dates, such as a rent-increase frequency limit, a notice period, a levy or a tax deductibility rule.
terms.label: Regulatory rule

terms.definition: A regulatory rule about income tax, capital gains tax, GST, land tax or duty that applies to a class of property or taxpayer from an effective date, possibly with a grandfathering cut-off.
terms.label: Tax rule

terms.definition: A numeric limit on residents, rooms, bedrooms, lettings or floor area that triggers, exempts or bounds the application of a regulatory regime.
terms.label: Occupancy threshold

terms.definition: A planning approval, building approval, fire-safety certification, registration, accreditation or licence issued by a government body to a party for a property or operation under a regulatory regime, with a status and validity.
terms.label: Authorisation

terms.definition: A development or use approval under a local planning scheme permitting a stated use (for example rooming accommodation) on a site, or an exemption from needing one.
terms.label: Planning approval

terms.definition: A building permit, classification change, occupancy approval or compliance notice confirming the building is approved for its intended class and use.
terms.label: Building approval

terms.definition: Documentation that the premises satisfy applicable fire-safety requirements (alarms, exits, emergency lighting, fire-safety management).
terms.label: Fire-safety certification

terms.definition: Queensland registration required before operating a residential service accommodating four or more residents who separately pay for accommodation.
terms.label: Residential service registration

terms.definition: Queensland accreditation of a registered residential service (Level 1 accommodation; Levels 2-3 where food or personal care are provided), sought within three months of registration.
terms.label: Accommodation service accreditation

terms.definition: The Victorian licence a person or entity must hold before operating a rooming house under the Rooming House Operators Act 2016; one licence can cover multiple premises.
terms.label: Rooming house operator licence

terms.definition: Victorian registration of each rooming-house premises with the local council under the public-health framework, separate from the operator licence.
terms.label: Rooming house premises registration

terms.definition: A state licence or registration held by a property agent, salesperson or corporation, recorded in a public register such as the Queensland Office of Fair Trading register.
terms.label: Real estate agent licence

terms.definition: A named approach to acquiring, holding, improving, operating or disposing of property to achieve return objectives (for example buy and hold, fix and flip, rooming house, dual income, small-scale development).
terms.label: Investment strategy

terms.definition: A named arrangement of who controls the asset, who earns the operating revenue and who bears vacancy and fixed-cost risk (ownership, master lease / rent-to-rent, management or revenue share, hybrid/franchise, corporate leasing, single-lease rental).
terms.label: Operating model

terms.definition: A named physical and occupancy configuration of accommodation (whole-house rental, rooming house / HMO, coliving, boarding house, share house, dual-income configurations, student accommodation, short-stay, single- or multi-tenant commercial).
terms.label: Accommodation type

terms.definition: A legal vehicle through which property is held (individual, joint tenants, tenants in common, discretionary trust, unit trust, company, self-managed super fund).
terms.label: Ownership structure

terms.definition: A stated tax, liability, distribution, financing, estate or administrative property of an ownership structure as described by a source.
terms.label: Structure characteristic

terms.definition: A named commercial or residential lease structure distinguished by duration and outgoings allocation (short-term, long-term, shopping-centre/retail, gross, net, triple net).
terms.label: Lease type

terms.definition: Whether a property is occupied by a single tenant or by multiple tenants under separate leases.
terms.label: Tenant configuration

terms.definition: A demand group that an accommodation product targets (students, young professionals, essential workers, corporate staff, singles and couples, families, new arrivals, temporary workers).
terms.label: Tenant segment

terms.definition: An organisational structure for a real-estate agency (franchise, cooperative, joint venture, boutique, independent) with characteristic control and capability-sourcing patterns.
terms.label: Agency business model

terms.definition: A National Construction Code building class (for example Class 1a, Class 1b, Class 3) that determines fire, egress and occupancy requirements.
terms.label: Building classification

terms.definition: A tax-law categorisation of a property activity or supply (rental investment, rental-property business, profit-making undertaking, input-taxed residential rent, commercial residential premises).
terms.label: Tax classification

terms.definition: The kind of authorisation a regime requires (planning approval, building approval, fire-safety certification, registration, accreditation, operator licence, premises registration, agent licence).
terms.label: Authorisation type

terms.definition: What an occupancy threshold counts: residents, unrelated tenants, rooms rented, bedrooms, separate lettings, persons, floor area, dwellings.
terms.label: Threshold kind

terms.definition: A named financial, operating or market measure (gross yield, net yield, NOI, cash-on-cash return, IRR, occupancy, economic vacancy, RevPAR, CAC, EBITDA, EBITDAR, DSCR, LVR, break-even occupancy, median rent, vacancy rate).
terms.label: Metric

terms.definition: A grouping of risks by nature (planning-use, building/fire, licensing, tenancy-law, vacancy/turnover, management intensity, insurance, interest-rate/refinancing, valuation/exit, construction-cost, tax-classification, policy, counterparty, market-cycle, data/privacy, key-person).
terms.label: Risk category

terms.definition: A category of property operating cost that a lease may allocate: taxes/rates, insurance, maintenance, common-area maintenance, capital expenditure, utilities.
terms.label: Outgoing category

terms.definition: The access model of a data source: open authoritative, public lookup or government paid, commercial API/extract, first-party, derived internally.
terms.label: Data access tier

terms.definition: A kind of information about a property that a data source can supply (address, parcel boundary, zoning, overlay, flood exposure, school catchment, transport access, demographics, development application, transaction, listing, rent, ownership, title, valuation).
terms.label: Property attribute

terms.definition: A named component that a business-planning artefact is recommended to contain (executive summary, market analysis, financial projections, risk and contingency, exit strategy, and so on).
terms.label: Document section

terms.definition: The way a property-management service is charged: percentage of rent collected, flat fee, hybrid, letting fee, renewal fee, ancillary fees.
terms.label: Fee model

terms.definition: How an organisation obtains a capability: owned internally, centralised, localised, outsourced, shared through a network, accessed through partnership (inbound/outbound open innovation).
terms.label: Capability sourcing

terms.definition: A category of property to which a tax rule applies: new residential build, established residential, commercial residential premises, build-to-rent project, affordable housing.
terms.label: Property class for tax purposes

terms.definition: A stage in a development or conversion project (acquisition screening, conditional due diligence, concept and approvals, construction, completion, operating approvals, lease-up, ongoing operation).
terms.label: Project phase

terms.definition: An uncertain event or condition that, if it occurs, adversely affects a strategy, operating model, agreement, property or project, categorised and optionally mitigated.
terms.label: Risk

terms.definition: A control, action or diligence step recorded as reducing the likelihood or impact of a risk.
terms.label: Mitigation

terms.definition: A go/no-go condition that must be satisfied before a project proceeds, such as the planning, building/fire, finance and operating gates for a rooming house.
terms.label: Decision gate

terms.definition: A document, dataset, model, plan, register or other information object produced or used in property business activity.
terms.label: Information artefact

terms.definition: An internal strategy document describing a business's objectives, structure, market, strategy, operations, finances, risks and exit.
terms.label: Business plan

terms.definition: A document describing a specific development project's site, scope, staging, milestones, team and delivery.
terms.label: Project plan

terms.definition: A financial and technical assessment of whether a site and project are viable, covering income and cost streams, structure, risks and projected position.
terms.label: Feasibility study

terms.definition: An external document (typically 25-30 pages) presenting a development to investors or lenders with overview, location, plan, team, market, financial plan, offer and risk management.
terms.label: Information memorandum

terms.definition: A projection artefact containing income statement, cash flow, balance sheet, sources and uses, break-even, ROI/IRR and sensitivity analysis.
terms.label: Financial model

terms.definition: A structured list of risks with owner, likelihood, impact, mitigation, trigger and response.
terms.label: Risk register

terms.definition: A dated milestone schedule with role matrix, approval gates, governance cadence and reporting.
terms.label: Implementation schedule

terms.definition: A document in the property-pages corpus (scraped article, government page, forum thread, academic paper, synthesis or report) from which claims are drawn.
terms.label: Source document

terms.definition: A published dataset, register, API or service that supplies property attributes, identifiers or market statistics for a jurisdiction under an access tier and licence.
terms.label: Data source

terms.definition: A documented operational process of a property business with trigger, responsible role, steps, decision points, records, service standard and escalation path.
terms.label: Workflow

terms.definition: A defined service a property-management business provides to landlords or tenants, such as tenant screening, lease preparation, rent collection, inspections, maintenance coordination or reporting.
terms.label: Service

terms.definition: A named set of underwriting assumptions applied to a property or project (project cost, leverage, interest, rooms, tariff, vacancy, operating-expense ratio, growth) that yields result metrics.
terms.label: Financial scenario

terms.definition: A value of a metric (numeric value, unit, basis note) as assumed in a scenario, computed as a result, or claimed by a source for a property, market or model.
terms.label: Metric value

terms.definition: An activity that acquires, converts, subdivides, builds or repositions property through phases from screening to operation, producing approvals, buildings and artefacts.
terms.label: Development project

terms.definition: The regulatory consequence when an occupancy threshold is satisfied: the regime applies in full, applies in part, does not apply, a permit is exempt, or an authorisation becomes required.
terms.label: Threshold effect

terms.definition: Links an agreement, property asset, development project or business to a participation in which a party bears a role in that context.
terms.label: has participation

terms.definition: The agreement, property asset, project or business in which the participation occurs.
terms.label: participation context

terms.definition: The party bearing the role in a participation.
terms.label: participant

terms.definition: The role borne by the participant in the participation.
terms.label: in role

terms.definition: Convenience shortcut stating the party that owns the property asset; equivalent in intent to a participation in the Owner role.
terms.label: owned by

terms.definition: Convenience shortcut stating the party that manages a property asset or portfolio on the owner's behalf.
terms.label: managed by

terms.definition: Convenience shortcut stating the party that operates accommodation at the property (the operator, provider or head tenant).
terms.label: operated by

terms.definition: The property asset (or rentable unit) that an agreement, authorisation, scenario, risk or project concerns.
terms.label: concerns asset

terms.definition: A clause contained in the agreement.
terms.label: has clause

terms.definition: The lease-type classification of an agreement.
terms.label: classified by lease type

terms.definition: Links a sublease to the head lease from which the operator's right to sublet derives.
terms.label: sublease under head lease

terms.definition: The accommodation type or use the agreement permits.
terms.label: permitted use

terms.definition: Links a lease type or agreement to an outgoing allocation.
terms.label: allocates outgoing

terms.definition: The category of outgoing being allocated.
terms.label: allocates outgoing category

terms.definition: The role (landlord/lessor or tenant/lessee) that bears the allocated outgoing.
terms.label: borne by role

terms.definition: The jurisdiction in which a property asset is located.
terms.label: located in

terms.definition: Containment of one jurisdiction within a larger one (a local government area within a state within a nation).
terms.label: within jurisdiction

terms.definition: A property identifier denoting the asset.
terms.label: has identifier

terms.definition: Mereological part relation between property assets (a room within a dwelling, a dwelling within a building, a building on a parcel).
terms.label: part of

terms.definition: The portfolio that holds or manages the asset.
terms.label: in portfolio

terms.definition: The ownership structure through which an asset or portfolio is held.
terms.label: held under ownership structure

terms.definition: A characteristic a source attributes to an ownership structure.
terms.label: has characteristic

terms.definition: The accommodation-type classification of a property asset or rentable unit.
terms.label: has accommodation type

terms.definition: The building-code class of a building or dwelling.
terms.label: has building classification

terms.definition: The operating model under which a property is, or is proposed to be, operated.
terms.label: intended operating model

terms.definition: Whether the property is single- or multi-tenant.
terms.label: uses tenant configuration

terms.definition: An authorisation held for, or required by, a property asset or party.
terms.label: has authorisation

terms.definition: The kind of authorisation.
terms.label: has authorisation type

terms.definition: The government body that issues or grants the authorisation.
terms.label: issued by

terms.definition: The party to whom the authorisation is granted (the operator, provider, licensee or applicant).
terms.label: authorised party

terms.definition: The regulatory regime under which the authorisation is issued or the rule sits.
terms.label: under regime

terms.definition: The jurisdiction in which a regulatory regime or rule applies.
terms.label: applies in

terms.definition: The legislation that establishes the regime or rule.
terms.label: governed by

terms.definition: The regulator or government body that administers the regime.
terms.label: administered by

terms.definition: An operating model to which the regime applies.
terms.label: applies to operating model

terms.definition: An accommodation type to which the regime applies.
terms.label: applies to accommodation type

terms.definition: A kind of authorisation that must be obtained before operating under the regime.
terms.label: requires authorisation type

terms.definition: An occupancy or size threshold that triggers, exempts or bounds the regime.
terms.label: has threshold

terms.definition: What the threshold counts.
terms.label: has threshold kind

terms.definition: A specific rule within the regime.
terms.label: has rule

terms.definition: The class of property (new build, established, commercial residential, build-to-rent) to which a tax rule applies.
terms.label: applies to property class

terms.definition: The tax classification attributed to an activity, party, property or supply.
terms.label: has tax classification

terms.definition: A prescribed form required by the regime for an agreement or notice.
terms.label: prescribes form

terms.definition: An operating model on which the investment strategy relies.
terms.label: strategy uses operating model

terms.definition: An accommodation type on which the investment strategy relies.
terms.label: strategy uses accommodation type

terms.definition: A tenant segment that a strategy, accommodation type or property targets.
terms.label: targets tenant segment

terms.definition: The investment strategy applied to a portfolio, asset or project.
terms.label: has strategy

terms.definition: A risk that applies to the subject (strategy, operating model, agreement, property, project or business).
terms.label: has risk

terms.definition: The category of the risk.
terms.label: classified in risk category

terms.definition: A mitigation recorded for the risk.
terms.label: mitigated by

terms.definition: A decision gate that must be passed for the subject (strategy or project).
terms.label: has decision gate

terms.definition: An authorisation type whose confirmation satisfies the decision gate.
terms.label: gate requires authorisation type

terms.definition: A metric value describing the subject (property, portfolio, market claim, scenario).
terms.label: has metric value

terms.definition: A metric value used as an input assumption of the scenario.
terms.label: assumes

terms.definition: A metric value produced as a result of the scenario.
terms.label: yields

terms.definition: The metric that the value measures.
terms.label: measures metric

terms.definition: The corpus source document that asserts the value, definition or claim.
terms.label: asserted in

terms.definition: The jurisdiction a metric value, claim or data source refers to.
terms.label: describes jurisdiction

terms.definition: The operating model or accommodation type that the scenario underwrites.
terms.label: scenario for operating model

terms.definition: A document section that a source or template recommends the artefact contain.
terms.label: recommends section

terms.definition: A service provided by the business.
terms.label: provides service

terms.definition: The fee model under which a service is charged.
terms.label: has fee model

terms.definition: A workflow that delivers the service.
terms.label: supported by workflow

terms.definition: A metric used as a key performance indicator for the business, service or workflow.
terms.label: measured by

terms.definition: The agency business model under which the business is organised.
terms.label: business model

terms.definition: The capability-sourcing pattern characteristic of the business model or business.
terms.label: sources capability via

terms.definition: The organisation that publishes the data source or document.
terms.label: published by

terms.definition: A property attribute the data source can supply.
terms.label: supplies attribute

terms.definition: The access tier of the data source.
terms.label: access tier

terms.definition: The jurisdiction the data source covers.
terms.label: covers jurisdiction

terms.definition: A phase of the development project.
terms.label: has phase

terms.definition: Ordering between project phases.
terms.label: precedes

terms.definition: An information artefact produced by the project or business activity.
terms.label: produces artefact

terms.definition: The investment strategy that the development project implements.
terms.label: project uses strategy

terms.definition: The regime application effect when the threshold is met (regime applies in full, applies in part, does not apply, permit exempt, licence required).
terms.label: has threshold effect

terms.definition: Rent payable per week under an agreement or for a rentable unit, in AUD unless stated.
terms.label: weekly rent

terms.definition: Scheduled rent per year.
terms.label: annual rent

terms.definition: Duration of an agreement in months.
terms.label: term (months)

terms.definition: Annual rent escalation rate in percent under an agreement.
terms.label: escalation rate (%)

terms.definition: Whether the rent obligation is fixed irrespective of occupancy (true for head/master leases).
terms.label: fixed rent regardless of occupancy

terms.definition: Date from which an agreement, authorisation, rule or regime is in force.
terms.label: effective from

terms.definition: Date until which an agreement, authorisation, rule or regime is in force.
terms.label: effective until

terms.definition: A grandfathering or eligibility cut-off date-time attached to a rule (for example 7:30 pm AEST 12 May 2026).
terms.label: cut-off date

terms.definition: Comparison operator for the threshold value: 'gte', 'lte', 'gt', 'lt', 'eq', 'range'.
terms.label: threshold comparator

terms.definition: Numeric threshold value (lower bound for ranges).
terms.label: threshold value

terms.definition: Upper bound when the comparator is 'range'.
terms.label: threshold upper value

terms.definition: Unit of the threshold value (persons, rooms, bedrooms, lettings, m2).
terms.label: threshold unit

terms.definition: The numeric value of a metric value.
terms.label: numeric value

terms.definition: Upper bound of a metric value reported as a range.
terms.label: upper value

terms.definition: Unit of a metric value (percent, AUD, AUD_per_week, months, ratio, EUR).
terms.label: unit

terms.definition: Free-text statement of the basis, assumptions or qualification attached to a value or claim.
terms.label: basis note

terms.definition: Date on which a claim or figure was published or is current.
terms.label: claim date

terms.definition: Number of separately lettable rooms or studios in a property.
terms.label: room count

terms.definition: Number of bedrooms.
terms.label: bedroom count

terms.definition: Total floor area in square metres.
terms.label: floor area (m2)

terms.definition: Land area in square metres.
terms.label: lot size (m2)

terms.definition: The literal value of a property identifier.
terms.label: identifier value

terms.definition: Short code for a jurisdiction (AU, QLD, VIC, NSW, WA, SA, BCC, LOGAN).
terms.label: jurisdiction code

terms.definition: Status of an authorisation: 'held', 'pending', 'expired', 'refused', 'not_required', 'unknown'.
terms.label: authorisation status

terms.definition: Date the authorisation was issued.
terms.label: date issued

terms.definition: How often a data source is updated (daily, weekly, quarterly, annual, release-driven, near-real-time).
terms.label: refresh cadence

terms.definition: Licence or terms under which a data source or document is available.
terms.label: licence note

terms.definition: Original location of a source document or data source.
terms.label: source URL

terms.definition: Date the artefact was published or compiled.
terms.label: publication date

terms.definition: Authority level of a source document: normative, authoritative, primary, secondary, expert, reference, illustrative.
terms.label: authority level

terms.definition: Human-readable name of a financial scenario (conservative, moderate, aggressive).
terms.label: scenario name

terms.definition: Text of a structure characteristic as stated by the source.
terms.label: characteristic note

terms.definition: Text describing the mitigation, control or diligence step.
terms.label: mitigation note

terms.definition: Text of the condition a decision gate requires.
terms.label: gate condition

terms.definition: Ordinal position of a project phase.
terms.label: phase order

terms.definition: Management fee expressed as a percentage of rent collected.
terms.label: fee (% of rent)

terms.definition: Number of properties under management or held.
terms.label: portfolio size (properties)

terms.definition: Roles a party can bear.
terms.label: Role scheme

terms.definition: Party holding legal ownership of the asset.
terms.label: Owner

terms.definition: Party deploying capital into property for return.
terms.label: Investor

terms.definition: Party running the accommodation business at the property (master tenant, rooming-house operator, coliving operator).
terms.label: Operator

terms.definition: Queensland term for the party providing rooming accommodation to residents.
terms.label: Provider (rooming accommodation)

terms.definition: Party granting the right to occupy under an agreement.
terms.label: Landlord / lessor

terms.definition: Party taking the right to occupy under a tenancy or lease.
terms.label: Tenant / lessee

terms.definition: Occupant of a room under rooming accommodation or coliving arrangements.
terms.label: Resident

terms.definition: Owner who lives at the property while renting rooms.
terms.label: Owner-occupier

terms.definition: Licensed party managing property for an owner.
terms.label: Property manager

terms.definition: Party providing debt finance secured on the property.
terms.label: Lender

terms.definition: Party insuring the property or business.
terms.label: Insurer

terms.definition: Party undertaking a development project.
terms.label: Developer

terms.definition: Planner, lawyer, accountant, building surveyor, valuer or other professional adviser.
terms.label: Adviser

terms.definition: Company leasing residential property for staff.
terms.label: Corporate tenant

terms.definition: Major tenant whose presence draws traffic and underpins co-tenancy clauses.
terms.label: Anchor tenant

terms.definition: Local government in its regulatory role.
terms.label: Council

terms.definition: Named investment strategies described in the corpus.
terms.label: Investment strategy scheme

terms.definition: Long-term ownership for capital growth and rental income.
terms.label: Buy and hold

terms.definition: Acquire undervalued property, renovate quickly, sell for gain.
terms.label: Fix and flip
